subject: Urgent: Offline hotfix delivery & dual-signature courier checklist
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-01T08:14:00Z
Subject: Urgent: Offline hotfix delivery & dual-signature courier checklist

Team,

We have an urgent patch (hotfix_v3.2) that must be applied to the air-gapped Acme Health cluster this week due to an edge-case KV-cache corruption that's causing 5XXs. Acme asked for an offline delivery (no inbound network) and will only accept media with dual-signature provenance. They also require an operator-level verification checklist and a signed chain-of-custody from the courier.

I sketched a minimally invasive plan — want review and sign-off before I loop in Acme and procurement: 

- Build: release team produces hotfix bundle: hotfix_v3.2_bundle.tar (signed by our release HSM key + ephemeral offline signing token).
- Manifest: manifest_v3.2.json contains SHA256 blobs, build metadata, RFC-style release notes excerpt. Manifest must itself be HSM-signed (detached sig).
- Dual-signature: primary sig = release HSM (redwood-release-hsm), secondary sig = lead engineer PGP-signed (operator PGP key). Both signatures accompany the bundle.
- Packaging: bundle + manifest + operator verification checklist + Ops runbook on USB (FIPS 140-validated encrypted container).
- Transport: SecureShip picks up from our secure facility; courier provides a signed PDF chain_of_custody at handoff and a tamper-evident seal id.
- On-site acceptance: Acme's on-site operator will verify the manifest SHA sums and both signatures using the provided tooling (we include an airgapped signature verification CLI).
- Emergency rollback: if verification fails, courier returns media and we initiate remote-signed rollback artifact via same flow.

Open questions I want resolved before external comms: 
1) Does release HSM policy allow generating the detached manifest signature for offline delivery? (Karthik)
2) Do we need an additional notarization step (DocuSign) for the courier handoff to satisfy Acme legal? (Laura)
3) Are operators comfortable with the offline verification CLI and the checksum steps? (Priyom / Marissa)

Please reply inline with any constraints or missing steps. If you approve, I'll prepare the delivery packet and loop in SecureShip + Acme SecOps.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-01T11:06:00Z
Subject: Re: Urgent: Offline hotfix delivery & dual-signature courier checklist

Jonas,

Thanks — high level looks good. A couple of practical items from Ops/security perspective: 

- HSM policy: we can produce a detached signature but we must avoid exporting any private key material. Karthik, can you confirm we can create the detached manifest sig with the release HSM without adding an additional approval flow that would delay pickup by >24h?

- Operator CLI: I've attached (referenced) the verification CLI binary and a short README. The CLI will validate: manifest sig (HSM sig), PGP operator sig, and SHA256 of the tar. We should include a small troubleshooting doc for common failure states (wrong timezone on airgapped box, missing libs).

- Tamper-evident seals: require unique seal id in chain_of_custody. SecureShip needs to include pre-printed seal IDs in their print run so Acme can validate against manifest.

- Legal: Laura — Acme requested DocuSign for acceptance sign-off. For emergency patch deliveries, can we get a one-click acceptance template? Otherwise procurement/legal will need to sign each pickup which slows the handoff.

If no blockers from Karthik/Laura/ Priyom by EOD I approve draft and we'll contact SecureShip and Acme SecOps.

- Marissa

Attachments: verification_cli_v1.4.tar.gz (binary archive)
From: SecureShip Ops <ops@secureship.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-02T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Pickup confirmation & chain of custody process (SecureShip)

Jonas / Marissa / Laura,

Thanks for the heads-up. We can support the pickup window on Nov 3 (0900-1200 local). Our standard air-gapped courier flow for encrypted media: 

- Handoff: Redwood ops signs internal pickup form; SecureShip driver signs and scans ID. Driver presents QR-coded manifest receipt at pickup and records GPS/time in our sealed courier ledger.
- Tamper seals: We'll supply tamper-seal batch S3-TS-20271103 with pre-printed IDs. We will affix a seal to each encrypted container and record its ID in the ledger.
- Chain doc: We'll provide a signed PDF chain_of_custody that includes: pickup signer, driver id, seal id(s), pickup timestamp, courier manifest hash. We will also include a notarized courier attestation for high-sensitivity deliveries (extra fee).
- Emergency return: If Acme refuses acceptance, driver will reseal and return to Redwood; we provide real-time return ETA and signed return receipt.

Required from Redwood before pickup: 
1) Pickup authorization PDF signed by Redwood legal or delegated approver (Laura?)
2) Copy of manifest_v3.2.json and the release manifest hash (SHA256) emailed to ops@secureship.com prior to driver dispatch (we will not hold copy at our endpoint).
3) Contact at Acme (name + phone) who will accept and sign on delivery.

We can attach our sample chain_of_custody PDF and our standard handling SOW. Pricing and notarization options attached.

Regards,
SecureShip Logistics
ops@secureship.com
Attachment: secure_ship_coc_sample.pdf, secureship_sow.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, ops@secureship.com
Date: 2027-11-03T16:32:00Z
Subject: Re: Urgent: Offline hotfix delivery & dual-signature courier checklist

Thanks everyone — quick decisions below so we can move to pickup: 

- Karthik: confirmed offline HSM detached signature possible with a single release operator approval; will run the sig job tonight (no key export).
- Laura: legal agreed to a delegated pickup authorization template for emergency patches; I'll sign on behalf of Product Security and Laura will countersign DocuSign after pickup acceptance.
- Priyom/Marissa: Ops verified the CLI and troubleshooting doc; on-site operator kit finalized.
- SecureShip: pickup confirmed Nov 3 09:30, they will include S3-TS-20271103 seals and a notarized courier attestation (we accepted the fee).

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Release: produce hotfix_v3.2_bundle.tar (Karthik) — due 2027-11-02 23:00Z.
- Security: produce detached manifest_sigs and operator PGP sigs (Jonas/Karthik) — due 2027-11-02 23:30Z.
- Legal: upload signed pickup authorization to SecureShip (Laura) — due 2027-11-03 05:00Z.
- Ops: prepare operator kit + verification_cli + runbook on encrypted USB (Marissa/Priyom) — due 2027-11-03 07:30Z.
- Logistics: SecureShip to pick up 2027-11-03 09:30 local; provide chain_of_custody PDF at handoff.

I'll notify Acme SecOps now and share the manifest hash and pickup ETA. If anyone sees a blocker, flag immediately in this thread.

Jonas
Head of Product Security | Redwood Inference
Attachments: hotfix_v3.2_bundle.tar.sig, manifest_v3.2.json, courier_chain_of_custody.pdf
